chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Bakr ibn Salih, from Sulayman al-Ja'fari, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) who said:
I heard him say: 'I do not eat the meat of the Bakhati, nor do I command anyone to eat it,' in a long hadith.

Because his saying (peace be upon him) 'I do not eat it' is a statement of his abstaining from eating it, and his saying 'I do not command' is merely a negation that it is something commanded, and if it were so, eating it would be obligatory, and that is not a statement to anyone. And in the report it is not that it is forbidden nor permissible, so it would not contradict the first report. On the other hand, the prohibition of the meat of the Bakhati was something the companions of Abu al-Khattab (may God curse them) used to say, so it is permissible that Sulayman al-Ja'fari heard one of his companions say it and narrated it from Abu al-Hasan based on conjecture rather than knowledge. And that which indicates that this was their saying is what he narrated:

key_terms.ظَنًّا لَا عِلْمًا: Based on conjecture rather than knowledge
key_terms.لُحُومُ الْبَخَاتِيِّ: Meat of the Bakhati (a specific type of fish or animal)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on eating the meat of the Bakhati according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Rida (AS) clarifies the legal status of 'Bakhati' meat, distinguishing between personal abstention (karaahat or sunnah) and definitive prohibition (haram), thereby refuting the specific view of the Abu al-Khattab school. The commentary highlights the methodological rigor of Shia hadith criticism, noting that Sulayman al-Ja'fari may have transmitted this ruling based on conjecture rather than certain knowledge, illustrating the importance of verifying the chain of transmission and the specific context of companion opinions in deriving fiqh.
